gap: No result ChatGPT got explains that the Manfrotto Befree Advanced's 9 kg rating is a 'Safety Payload' certified under UNI/PdR 105:2021. That rating means the loaded head must not slip out in any position it can take, including portrait, and the leg sections, center column and spider must not collapse. Peak Design's '20 pound weight capacity' and SIRUI's '4 kg max load' come with no published test method, so the three numbers on ChatGPT's cards don't measure the same thing.
standout_why: I compared this against Finding the Universe (cited), DPReview (rank 5), best-tripod.com (rank 9) and Digital Camera World (cited). Finding the Universe says only that 'load ratings aren't standardised between brands' and doesn't name the standard or what it guarantees. DPReview lists 8 / 9.1 kg load limits and says nothing about how they were measured. best-tripod.com uses the words 'safety payload' for the Manfrotto and Gitzo but never defines them or names UNI/PdR 105:2021. The Digital Camera World page returned no body text. None of these pages says what the certified rating actually promises (no head slip in any position, no leg or column collapse) or contrasts it with an untested 'max payload'.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's pick of the Manfrotto Befree Advanced for a DSLR. Its 9 kg is the only rating among the candidates certified to cover every head position, including tipping a front-heavy DSLR and lens into portrait. Peak Design's 20 lb looks like twice the capacity, but nobody has published how it was measured, so it can't be compared directly. DPReview also found the Peak Design head's claws get in the way of portrait shooting at some angles. The SIRUI Traveler 5C's 4 kg max load is the tightest of the three for a DSLR with a 70-200 f/2.8.

findings.source_title: Befree Advanced AS twist carbon tripod | Manfrotto US
findings.note: The maker's US product page lists the rating under UNI/PdR 105:2021. On the same page: ball head 'Advanced 494', 200PL PRO plate (Arca-type compatible), 4 sections, tubes 11.2–21.7 mm.

findings.label: Max height / max height with center column down / closed length / weight
findings.source_title: Befree Advanced AS twist carbon tripod | Manfrotto US
findings.note: With the center column down, the tripod reaches 50 in. Finding the Universe recommends keeping the column down for stability.

findings.label: What a UNI/PdR 105:2021 Safety Payload guarantees
findings.value: Manfrotto: 'a support loaded with a weight equal to the declared Safety Payload is never jeopardised, no matter the position'. The head 'must never slip out of the docking seat in any position the head can take'. The 'telescopic leg sections, center column and spider of the tripod must never collapse'.
findings.source_title: Your equipment safer than ever | Manfrotto
findings.note: This is the maker describing the standard in its own words. The page does not give the lab procedure or a safety factor beyond 'strict lab tests that take multiple factors into account'.

findings.label: Max Payload vs Safety Payload
findings.value: Manfrotto: 'Max Payload indicates the maximum load a support can hold, sometimes not taking safety parameters into account.'
findings.source_title: Your equipment safer than ever | Manfrotto
findings.note: Manfrotto defines this for its own ratings. It explains why a 'max load' number from any maker isn't directly comparable with a certified safety payload.

findings.label: Stated capacity and test basis
findings.value: '20 pound weight capacity'; 'Built for use with full frame DSLRs and telephoto lenses'
findings.note: The page says only that '3rd party testing shows' it performs as well as or better than bulkier tripods. It names no lab, standard or head position for the 20 lb figure. Weights on the same page: carbon 1.29 kg (2.81 lb), aluminum 1.56 kg (3.44 lb).

findings.label: Portrait-orientation clearance (DPReview)
findings.value: DPReview found the head's claws 'interfere both with portrait-orientation shooting at some angles'
findings.source_title: Tested: Four travel tripods for every budget | DPReview
findings.note: Hands-on test from 2020. DPReview's own measurements in the same piece: column-down height 131.0 cm for Peak Design and 127.0 cm for the Manfrotto BeFree Advanced. This page was already among ChatGPT's results.

findings.label: Max load / weight / folded length / max height
findings.note: This is a 'max load' figure with no test standard named. Also listed: 5 leg sections, tubes 10–22 mm, minimum height 160 mm.
